text:
maya: heads up — after landing kernel-selector=cost-based-v2 for the int8 runtime we see steady GPU memory growth on long-context runs (~20–30k tokens). KV pages are being paged/evicted but total mem still climbs. attaching quick traces below.

jonathan: can you paste the config you used? model, batch heuristic, kv_page_size, warmup steps etc?

maya: model: raven-13b-int8-dropin; kernel_selector=cost-based-v2; batching: max_batch_tokens=4096, active_window_ms=15; kv_page_size=16MB; kv_warmup_steps=32

lucy: hmm. do you see page.refcount spikes? last time we saw similar behavior it was because warmup left transient refs on pages until compaction ran.

maya: profiler dump (snip):
```
NVML GPU0 mem used: 4.2G -> 5.1G -> 6.0G -> 6.9G (over 10k tokens)
KV pages allocated: 48 -> 56 -> 64
KV pages evicted: 12 -> 18
page_compactions: 0
```

lucy: that page_compactions:0 is suspicious. cost-based-v2 seems to prefer larger kernel tiling that keeps multiple kv page views alive for reuse. with int8 we also have the quantized-kv cache mappings which add shadow refs.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: int8-warmup-kernel-v2 (nightly) — p95 latency +11.7%, GPU mem growth flagged (leak-like). See CI: //ci/perf/179900

jonathan: quick experiment: try toggling kernel_selector=latency-first or enable page-compact-on-evict=true. can you repro with a short script?

maya: repro script attached (small loop sending 8k token prefixes repeatedly). repro in ~45s on devbox. toggling page-compact-on-evict=true stops long-term growth, drop p95 back to baseline. but throughput drops ~6%.

karen: Is the tradeoff acceptable? SLA teams will care about p95 vs mem. we should canary the revert or enable compaction as opt-in flag per-customer.

lucy: also need to measure accuracy/regression from int8 drop-in. early eval shows ~0.4% exact-match drop on our eval set after warmup differences (likely from kernel tiling + quantization rounding). not huge but visible.

maya: commands I ran:
```
# repro
python tools/repro_kv_growth.py --model raven-13b-int8 --kernel-selector cost-based-v2 --kv-page-size 16MB --loop-steps 500
# toggle
redwoodctl config set runtime.kernel_selector=latency-first --env dev
redwoodctl config set runtime.kv.page_compact_on_evict=true
```

jonathan: next steps I propose:
- write minimal unit reproducer for infra tests (maya)
- add page.refcount hist and compact-run to nightly (lucy)
- run int8 accuracy sweep with and without compaction/kernel changes (karen)
- consider making compaction a low-cost async background worker rather than sync on-evict (perf)

maya: i've pushed repro and flamegraph to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/179900_kv_warmup_int8/ (link)

perf-bot: scheduled job perf/longctx-int8/179900-repro on infra-ml-large (ETA 1h)

lucy: quick note — there's also a KV packing shadow buffer used for int8->fp16 touches. if kernel-selector chooses larger tile widths we end up materializing more shadow slices which prevents freeing underlying pages until GC. adding a small test that forces tile_width=32 reduces shadow materialization and seems to help.

maya: good find. i'll test tile_width knob next.

karen: if we can make compaction async + tile_width fallback for long-context customers, we can avoid revert. but plan B is to rollback cost-based-v2 for int8 until we have automated compaction.

jonathan: agree. please log the rollback signal thresholds (mem growth > 800MB over 5m OR p95 +>10%) so SRE can auto-signal a canary stop.

maya: will do. thanks everyone. I'll update this thread after the tile_width run and the perf job results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lucy: :eyes:

infra-bot: action items created: PERF-4123 (repro + nightly hist), RUNTIME-2891 (async compaction design)

maya: (reacts :thumbsup:)
